question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India provides for Fundamental Rights?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Articles 12 to 35**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Fundamental Rights** are enshrined in **Part III** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• These rights are provided under **Articles 12 to 35**.
 
• Fundamental Rights guarantee civil liberties to all citizens of India, ensuring equality, freedom, and justice.
 
• Key Fundamental Rights include:
 
 
• The **Right to Equality** (Articles 14-18).
 
• The **Right to Freedom** (Articles 19-22).
 
• The **Right against Exploitation** (Articles 23-24).
 
• The **Right to Freedom of Religion** (Articles 25-28).
 
• The **Cultural and Educational Rights** (Articles 29-30).
 
• The **Right to Constitutional Remedies** (Article 32).
 
 
 
• These rights are justiciable, meaning individuals can approach the courts if their Fundamental Rights are violated.
 
• The **Supreme Court** and **High Courts** have the power to enforce these rights through writs like habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, and certiorari.
 
• The Fundamental Rights are inspired by the **United States Bill of Rights**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Articles 15 to 35**__

 __
 
• This option is incorrect because **Articles 15 to 35** cover only a part of the Fundamental Rights.
 
• While some Fundamental Rights like the **Right to Equality** and **Right to Freedom** are included here, **Articles 12-14** are also essential for defining Fundamental Rights.
 
 
 
• **Articles 2 to 7**__
 __
 
• **Articles 2 to 7** are related to provisions regarding the **admission of new states** or **alteration of areas, boundaries, or names of existing states**.
 
• These articles are not related to Fundamental Rights but to the organization of states in India.
 
 
 
• **Articles 10 to 40**__
 
 
• **Articles 10 to 40** do not exclusively deal with Fundamental Rights.
 
• They include provisions such as **citizenship** and **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP).**
 
• **Directive Principles** (Articles 36-51) are non-justiciable guidelines to the State, unlike Fundamental Rights, which are justiciable.
